# `PiStatus`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Sparse delta of device power and thermal status (SoC temperature, battery, charger, Type-C).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | event (device sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, CPiStatusChecker::DoNotify @0x1275c0, FormatStatus @0x126d90, RefreshPiTemp @0x137790, TypecChange @0x127770, BatteryChange @0x12b3e0 (no model branch) (64-bit build); BatteryChange @0xb47f4 (model check @0xb4c04, 3.1 V literal @0xb4e10) (32-bit build); temp-only and battery_temp-only shapes OBSERVED (2026-10-12) |

Broadcast to all retained sockets on TCP 4700 (channel I) by the status checker when its internal changed-field list is non-empty. Each event carries only the members whose fields changed since the last delta, each at most once even when changed several times; the list is then cleared. The changed list itself is never sent, and there is no state, code, error or result wrapper. Merge each event into retained state; pi_get_info and the pi_status member of get_device_state give the full snapshot and do not consume a pending delta. Triggers: a poll loop that sleeps one second per pass marks temp changed only when it differs from the retained baseline by more than 1.0 degree C (the baseline is not advanced for smaller changes, so several sub-degree drifts can eventually trigger) or when is_overtemp changes, and also reads battery and charger status; the Type-C callback notifies immediately on a changed boolean. The formatter has no timer or throttle, so neither exactly one event per second nor a 1 Hz maximum is a protocol guarantee. A changed-list entry for an unrecognized field produces no member, so an envelope-only PiStatus is possible in principle. The 32-bit build serializes the same nine members. The member set does not depend on the model; the model only changes the low-battery shutdown voltage on the 32-bit build (3.1 V on S50, 3.25 V otherwise). The builds read different charger chips, so the charger_status mapping may differ by build, not by model. APK consumer expectation (not emitted): the app status DTOs also declare is_undervolt and is_over_current, and the checker has voltage/current tracking helpers, but neither build serializes these keys. Observation (2026-10-12): 29 PiStatus events in 300 s on a device imaging a plan, carrying temp only, at intervals of 1.0 to 44.6 s; another capture carried battery_temp only.

Side effects: Observation only.

## Request params

None. Events are sent by the device without a request; the payload is below.

## Payload

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Event` | string | yes | - | Discriminator. Fixed value `"PiStatus"`. [READ] |
| `Timestamp` | string | yes | - | Decimal string with nine fractional digits from a monotonic clock; not a calendar time. [READ] |
| `is_overtemp` | boolean | if field changed | - | SoC over-temperature flag (threshold crossing). [READ] |
| `temp` | number | if field changed | - | SoC thermal-zone temperature in degrees C (sensor value divided by 1000). [READ] |
| `charger_status` | string | if field changed | - | Charger state with initial capital. Derived from the charger's own status, battery_temp and battery_capacity. Discharging and Unknown pass through; Full is kept only at 100 percent capacity, otherwise Charging; any other status is decided by battery_temp T (T <= 0 Cold, T <= 10 Cool, 45 <= T <= 49 Warm, T > 49 Hot, otherwise Charging, or Full at 100 percent). The charger's not-charging status is never reported. The builds read different charger chips, so the mapping may differ by build, not by model. Clients SHOULD compare case-insensitively. One of: `Charging`, `Discharging`, `Full`, `Cool`, `Warm`, `Cold`, `Hot`, `Unknown`. [READ (vendor charger-library part from an archived copy not proven identical to 9.31)] |
| `battery_capacity` | integer | if field changed | - | Battery capacity; percent INFERRED. [READ; unit INFERRED] |
| `charge_online` | boolean | if field changed | - | Charger online flag. [READ] |
| `is_typec_connected` | boolean | if field changed | - | Type-C connection flag; the Type-C callback notifies immediately. [READ] |
| `battery_overtemp` | boolean | if field changed | - | Battery over-temperature flag. [READ] |
| `battery_temp` | integer | if field changed | - | Battery (charger) temperature as reported by the charger driver's power-supply sysfs temp attribute, an unscaled integer in whole degrees C. The 64-bit build reads it through the vendor charge library, the 32-bit build reads a different charger chip's sysfs file directly. [READ (source, no scaling); unit INFERRED (from the device's own thresholds)] |
| `battery_temp_type` | string | if field changed and the internal value is known | - | Battery temperature class; an unknown internal value emits no member. One of: `normal`, `high`, `low`. [READ] |

## Errors

None. Failures appear in the payload (`code`, `error`) when `state` is `fail`.

## Example

Event, temp-delta - Shape OBSERVED (2026-10-12); value invented:

```json
{"Event":"PiStatus","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","temp":47.2}
```

Event, battery-temp-delta - Shape OBSERVED (2026-10-12); value invented:

```json
{"Event":"PiStatus","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","battery_temp":31}
```

Event, typec-plugged - READ shape, not captured; values invented:

```json
{"Event":"PiStatus","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","is_typec_connected":true,"charge_online":true,"charger_status":"Charging"}
```
